A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TSNet/TS-GNN research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification experiments, including zero-shot comparisons in Table 1 and training-data-size results in Figure 3 and Appendix D.1.

after.justification: v3 retains the original TS-Mean and TS-GAT experiments and the training-data-size evaluation in Section 6 and Appendix D.1.

M1.justification: The TSNet/TS-GNN architecture, least-squares feature-label mixing, label projection, and scale-aware bias mechanism remain unchanged. The inpainting explanation and auxiliary projected-network definitions clarify the existing task and proof.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 29 node-classification datasets and retain the Cora-to-28-graphs evaluation and nine-graph training pool with 20 evaluation graphs. The new inpainting discussion does not introduce an evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains MeanGNN, GAT, and GraphAny alongside TS-Mean and TS-GAT. Figure 3 continues to compare TS-Mean with GraphAny; comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Official splits, PCA preprocessing, feature normalization, accuracy metrics, training subsets, and model configurations remain unchanged. Appendix Tables 4–6 retain the same training graphs and hyperparameter settings.

E4.justification: The training-data-size analysis in Section 6.2 and its per-dataset breakdown in Appendix D.1 are retained. Neither version contains additional ablations, robustness tests, or case studies absent from the other.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds, mean accuracy and standard deviation for Table 1, and five-seed averages for the scaling experiment. Uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain their numerical entries, and Figure 3 contains the identical plot. For example, Table 1 retains average accuracies of 65.78 ± 2.28 for TS-Mean and 65.56 ± 1.86 for GraphAny. Reported empirical findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 substantially revises the universality proof: it removes the approximator-definition requirement that N be contained in B, supplies the composition theorem's proof, and adds projected-network reconstruction and quotient-space lemmas. The final factor r is treated as continuous instead of necessarily polynomial. Conversely, v1 Appendix A.2's explicit proof of Proposition 4.1 is removed. The main universality statement and exclusion set are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: triple-symmetry characterization, universality on sets, a general TS-GNN recipe, zero-shot generalization, and improvement with additional training graphs.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds an explanation of fixed-label-set limitations and how partial test-graph labels enable label inpainting across unseen label sets. This clarifies applicability and prediction mechanisms. Existing exclusion-set qualifications, node-level scope, and lack of regression experiments remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The optimizer, single NVIDIA L40 GPU, preprocessing instructions, hyperparameter tables, and public implementation access information are retained. No implementation or resource-availability changes are documented.

R1.justification: v3 adds Smith's 2017 Groups and Their Representations lecture notes to support Appendix A.2. Positioning relative to GraphAny and the discussion of Maron et al. (2020) remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds a contents section and extensively rewrites and reorganizes the theoretical appendices. Appendix A becomes an expanded background primer, while Appendix B separates the earlier argument into thirteen subsections with additional explanations and intermediate statements. Section 4.1 also gains the label-inpainting exposition.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redrawn with grouped proof stages, revised dependencies, network labels, and caption. The contents section changes the opening layout, and retained tables and figures move with the reorganized text. Figures 1–3 and the empirical table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the universality argument easier to inspect and corrects the continuous-versus-polynomial function-class mismatch, while adding supporting proofs. However, it removes v1 Appendix A.2's explicit derivation of Proposition 4.1, a central claimed characterization, without a replacement derivation. With empirical evidence unchanged, these opposing effects on theoretical substantiation prevent a confident net quality judgment.
